newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ANDRETTI WINS MIAMI INDYCAR RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ANDRETTI WINS MIAMI INDYCAR RACE.

text.p: Michael Andretti won the IndyCar series-opening CART Grand Prix of Miami Sunday driving a Swift Ford -- the first victory for a U.S.-manufactured chassis since April of 1983.
Andretti, driving for the Newman/Haas team, beat Canadian Paul Tracy, who was in a Penske Mercedes-Benz, and 1996 series champion Jimmy Vasser, who drove a Reynard Honda.
Andretti's margin of victory was 4.2 seconds. Organisers, using a new timing system, still could not give clockings more than an hour and a half after the race ended.
Winning car owner Carl Haas severed his ties with Lola, a British company, at the end of last year to develop the Swift, designed by David Bruns, in San Clemente, California.
"I was very confident with this race car, I knew that David had designed winning cars in the past. With all the experience on the team I knew that we had a winning package," said Haas.

Remarkably, the win came in the first outing ever for the Swift chassis in the series. It was Andretti's second victory in a car debuting in the CART series. He also won introducing a Reynard Ford in Australia in 1994.
